label: Create Sketch
params: plane: XY|XZ|YZ (sketch x, y along world +X, +Y on XY; +X, -Z on XZ; +Y, +Z on YZ) | construction plane name or id | {origin?: [x,y,z] in mm, default [0,0,0], each a number or a length expression (an origin whose expressions name parameters is kept, and the sketch follows them when they change), x_dir, y_dir} (in world coordinates unless frame says otherwise; a named plane is the active component's own) | {face: [world x,y,z], body?: exact world body, index?: face index, path?: complete occurrence ids, fixed?: bool}; new face attachments require a unique certified source (a flat face of a sheet metal body attaches to its panel instead, in the flat pattern's coordinates), fixed:true explicitly freezes the selected plane; offset?: expr, flip?: bool | "x" | "y" (not on a face: sketch the plane from its other side, so the normal and the default extrude direction are reversed; a half turn about the plane's own x or y axis, true picks the one keeping the sketch's y axis upward; offset still moves along the unflipped normal), frame?: world (default) | component (which coordinates an explicit plane is in; the reply's `frame` says which, with a `note` when the active component is moved or turned), project_edges?: bool, activate_part?: bool (default false; on a face of a body of another component than the active one: activate that component at the picked placement first, as component.activate would, and make the sketch there; it stays active afterwards and the reply's `activated` names it), name?

label: Edit Sketch
params: sketch: id or name; restore_marker?: nonnegative timeline position, null (end) or false. A position or null: temporarily roll to this sketch and restore that position on Finish or Cancel; Finish groups the edit into one Undo step. Omitted: the same with the current position when features come after the sketch, so they rebuild once at Finish rather than after every sketch command. false: leave the timeline in place (later features rebuild after every sketch command)

label: Finish Sketch
params: restore_marker?: bool (default true); false transfers the temporary marker directly to another editor without rebuilding the intervening timeline

label: Cancel Sketch
params: Leaves the sketch without keeping what changed since it was created or opened for editing: the design goes back to how it was then (a new sketch is removed), as one step that Undo brings back. Refused when the undo history no longer leads back to that point (use Undo instead). restore_marker?: bool (default true); false transfers the temporary marker to another editor

label: Line
params: points: [[x,y] | "l1.end" | {at, ref}…] (x and y each a number or an expression over the design's parameters, "W / 2": such a point is fixed where it comes to and follows the parameters, while text naming no parameter, such as "5", is just that number, in the design's length unit (a JSON number is mm), and does not itself fix the point; likewise wherever a point argument also takes a point id), closed?: bool, construction?: bool, ids?: [..], infer?: bool (add horizontal/vertical); connect?: bool (default true: a new point landing exactly on an existing point, the origin too, is made coincident with it). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Draw Dimensioned Sketch Geometry
params: command: sketch creation command, params: object, dimensions: object of role to numeric or expression value, or `name = expression` (also `#name = expression`), which defines the user parameter `name` as sketch.dimension does (the reply's `defined` lists the names) (optional with as_drawn or locate), as_drawn?: bool (also dimension every other role of the shape at its size as drawn; a radius or diameter given takes the place of the other, as an edge polygon's side length does its radius, a circle otherwise takes its diameter, and a size the sketch already determines, such as the angle of a line inferred horizontal, is left out), locate?: bool (then place the shape from the sketch origin until nothing of it is left free: horizontal and vertical distances from the origin to its points, centres first, each kept only where it removes freedom, so a shape anchored to the origin or to placed geometry gets none; a point on an axis goes onto that axis instead of a 0 distance; the reply's located lists them); creates geometry and all driving dimensions atomically in one undo step. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: 2-Point Rectangle
params: p0, p1: opposite corners [x,y] (a coordinate may be an expression over the design's parameters: the corner is fixed and follows them; text naming no parameter, such as "5", is just that number, in the design's length unit (a JSON number is mm), and does not itself fix the corner); construction?. Returns sides {bottom, right, top, left} (line ids) and corners {bottom_left, bottom_right, top_right, top_left} (point ids); connect?: bool (default true: a new point landing exactly on an existing point, the origin too, is made coincident with it). label: 3-Point Rectangle

Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Rounded Rectangle
params: p0, p1: opposite corners [x,y] (a coordinate may be an expression over the design's parameters: the corner is fixed and follows them, as in `sketch.rectangle.two_point`; text naming no parameter, such as "5", is just that number, in the design's length unit (a JSON number is mm), and does not itself fix the corner); radius: expr (the corner radius, less than half the shorter side); construction?. A 2-point rectangle whose four corners are filleted alike: one radius dimension (`param`), the other arcs equal to it. Returns sides {bottom, right, top, left} (line ids) and arcs (the corner arcs: bottom-left, bottom-right, top-right, top-left), diagonal (construction, between the bottom-left and top-right arc centres) and centre (the point held at its midpoint); connect?: bool (default true: a new point landing exactly on an existing point, the origin too, is made coincident with it). Returns sides {bottom, right, top, left} (line ids) and corners {bottom_left, bottom_right, top_right, top_left} (point ids); connect?: bool (default true: a new point landing exactly on an existing point, the origin too, is made coincident with it). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Point
params: point: [x,y] (each a number or an expression over the design's parameters: the point is then fixed where it comes to and follows them; text naming no parameter, such as "5", is just that number, in the design's length unit (a JSON number is mm), and does not itself fix the point) or a snap: "mid:<line>" (held at the line's midpoint), "on:<curve>:x,y" (on the curve near x,y), "x:<a>+<b>:x,y" (at the crossing of two curves near x,y), {vertex: [x,y,z]} or {on_edge: [x,y,z]} of the model; id?; connect?: bool (default true: a new point landing exactly on an existing point, the origin too, is made coincident with it). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Sketch Dimension
params: entities: [refs] (3D sketch geometry too, #10608: a drawn 3D line for its length, two 3D points such as "w1.start" for their distance, with type distance_x / distance_y / distance_z for the run along an axis, two drawn 3D lines for the angle between them, a drawn 3D arc for its radius; driven and value work as below; a line midpoint is "mid:line_id"; a model edge or vertex, {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, is projected into the sketch first and measured there: a point against the projected edge measures the distance to it), type?: auto|distance|horizontal|distance_x|vertical|distance_y|length|radius|diameter|major|minor|angle, value?: number or expression (default: current; a bare number is in the design's units, e.g. 2 means 2 in in an inch design; give a unit such as "50 mm" to override), or `name = expression` (e.g. "width = 40"; also `#name = expression`), which adds the user parameter `name` with that expression and dimensions with `name` (refused when the name is taken or reserved; the reply's `defined` names it); text_at?: [x, y]. Two points or a line off the axes: with auto, text_at across from them (between the perpendiculars through them, or a tenth of their distance past) is the distance between them; pulled further past an end, up or down from it horizontal, sideways vertical. Two midpoints: placing text above or below their bounding box measures horizontally, beside it vertically, anywhere else (inside it or past its corners) the distance between them. Two lines: the angle between them (acute, or 180° − it when the value is nearer that) unless text_at picks a sector. A line and a circle or arc: the distance from the line to its edge (the gap, or how far the edge reaches past a line that cuts it; 0 is tangent); dimension the centre point for the distance to the centre. A point and a circle or arc: the distance from the point to its edge (or how far within it a point inside lies). Two circles or arcs: the gap between their edges (or how far they overlap when they cross, or the narrowest gap between them when one lies inside the other), or the centre-to-centre distance when they are the two caps of a slot. An ellipse: a half-axis, the distance from the centre to an axis end (major or minor; with auto, text_at pulled across the major axis gives the major half-axis, pulled out past an end of it the minor one, the minor without text_at; previous_axis?: major|minor, the half-axis an earlier placement chose, kept while text_at is near the boundary between them; the reply's axis names the one chosen; with auto, when a driving dimension already holds one half-axis (or its whole axis), the other one, wherever text_at is; without its major axis line the major half-axis goes to the ellipse's own major end, without its minor axis line the minor half-axis is the minor radius); any other type, radius among them, the minor radius; an ellipse's axis line with auto: its length, the whole axis, wherever text_at is; half_axes?: bool (default true; false: with auto, the minor radius wherever text_at is, as before half-axes, which the Dimension tool sends with Draw ellipses with their axes off). An arc and one of its end points: the arc's length (type arc_length does it from the arc alone). A dimension the sketch already determines is refused (naming what determines it); if_redundant?: "driven" places it as a driven (reference) dimension instead. scale_sketch?: bool (the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference, on by default): when this is the sketch's first length dimension and nothing in the sketch fixes a size (no other driving length dimension, nothing fixed or projected), the whole sketch scales to the value instead of distorting: about the origin when the drawing is tied to it (joined to the origin, or constrained to a sketch axis), otherwise about the middle of the drawing, so it stays where it was drawn (#11043); scale_about_origin?: bool (default false; the dimension tool sends the Sketch preference) scales about the origin always, as before #11043. Returns measured in unit (mm or deg), and scaled: the factor when the sketch was scaled

label: Horizontal/Vertical
params: line: id | points: [a, b] (point ids or {midpoint: line_id}; accepted midpoints reuse or create a point with a Midpoint constraint); mode?: horizontal|vertical

label: Coincident
params: a, b: points (or a line's middle as {midpoint: line}, which becomes a point tied there), a point and a curve or sketch axis (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created), or two distinct lines (joins their closest endpoints), or two circles/arcs (the second lies on the first: concentric and equal, `constraints` lists both); in a 3D sketch, two 3D points (`<3D curve>.start`, `.end`, `.through`, `.<n>`, or a 3D point's id) or a 3D point and a drawn 3D line; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Tangent
params: a, b: curves or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created), or the end point of a line or an arc: that end then lies on the other curve (or on the other end point), and its curve is tangent there, in one step (`constraints` lists both); in a 3D sketch, a drawn 3D line and a drawn 3D arc that meet at an end (the line leaves the arc the way it runs on); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Equal
params: a, b: lines or circles/arcs (in a 3D sketch, two drawn 3D lines or two drawn 3D arcs); or curves: [2 to 200 lines or circles/arcs], each made equal to the first, in one step; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Parallel
params: a, b: lines or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); in a 3D sketch, two drawn 3D lines, or a drawn 3D line and an origin plane xy / yz / xz; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Perpendicular
params: a, b: lines or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); in a 3D sketch, two drawn 3D lines; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Fix/Unfix
params: entity: point or curve | entities: [points and curves] (3D points and drawn 3D curves too, not mixed with planar ones); fixed?: bool (default: fix them all unless all are fixed, then unfix); unfixing a point placed by parameter expressions (`sketch.inspect` shows them as its `fixed_by`) frees it where they come to now, as plain numbers

label: MidPoint
params: point, line | a, b in pick order: a point and a line (either way round), or two lines whose midpoints meet (the first stays, the second moves); any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Concentric
params: a, b: two circles/arcs, or a circle/arc and a sketch point (including origin), in either order; the point and the curve's centre become coincident; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Collinear
params: a, b: lines or sketch axes (x / y: the sketch's own axes, unless a curve has that id; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); in a 3D sketch, two drawn 3D lines; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Symmetry
params: a, b: two points or two curves (lines mirror their ends, circles/arcs their centres); line: symmetry line id, or x / y for the sketch's own axes (a curve with that id wins; an axis becomes a linked construction line on it, reported in created); or point (or a point id as line, "origin" too): symmetric about that point, each pair joined by a construction line it is the midpoint of; any of them may be a model edge {edge: [x,y,z], body?} or vertex {vertex: [x,y,z], body?}, projected into the sketch first (reported in created)

label: Normal/Construction
params: curves: [ids], value?: bool (default: construction unless all of them already are)

label: Delete Sketch Entities
params: entities: [curve, point or constraint ids]

label: Drag Sketch Point
params: point: ref, to: [x,y]

label: Move Sketch Points
params: moves: [{point: ref | near: [x,y], to: [x,y]}] (each point to its own target; `near`: the sketch point closest to it, refused when none lies within `tolerance` or two are as close), tolerance?: mm (default 0.1); sketch? → moved: [{point, to, at, reached}] (`at`: where it ended up after the one solve; `reached`: whether that is `to`); a point placed by parameter expressions is refused, naming them (unfix it with sketch.constraint.fix first)

label: Drag Sketch Geometry
params: entity: point or curve, from: [x,y] where it was grabbed, to: [x,y], live?: bool: points and the material point grabbed on a line move toward `to` within the design constraints. When exact placement is impossible, bounded feasible steps minimize cursor distance. Splines slide by to - from; a circle or arc grabbed on its edge takes the radius to `to`. `with?`: [point or curve ids] moves the rest of a selection with the entity as one translation (circles keep their radii). Long moves retain the solution branch; arcs cannot sweep through their starts. Returns `reached`: progress projected onto the requested move (0..1), `at`: the grabbed position for the next frame, and `retry`: budget-limited progress can continue in another frame. `live: true` shares a work budget across held-solve decomposition and cursor correction; ordinary recovery and the final model evaluation retain their existing limits, not a wall-clock deadline. Later features stay stale until `sketch.drag_end`; `dof` stays from before the drag

label: End Sketch Drag
params: constraint?: {command: a sketch.constraint.* id, params}: ends a drag made of `sketch.drag` `live: true` frames: adds the constraint it let go on (not kept if it over-constrains the sketch), then evaluates the whole model once; returns the constraint's result and the sketch's solved state and degrees of freedom

label: Move Dimension Text
params: dimension: constraint id or parameter name; at: [x,y] text centre (sketch coordinates) | reset: true (default place)

label: Sketch Palette Options
params: sketch?: id|name (default active); any of show_profile, show_points, show_dimensions, show_constraints, show_projected, show_construction, grid, snap, slice, sketch_3d: bool. Returns them all

label: Chain
params: curve: id: the curves joined to it end to end (what a double-click selects)

label: Solve Sketch
params: reports the solver status and degrees of freedom

label: Midpoint Line
params: mid: [x,y], point ref or snap ("mid:<line>", "on:<curve>:x,y", model vertex/edge); end: [x,y]; construction?. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Tangent Arc
params: start: end point of a line or arc ("l1.end"), end: [x,y] or an existing point's id ("l2.start": the arc ends on that point); curve?: the curve to be tangent to (default: the one ending at start). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: 2-Tangent Circle
params: curves: [two lines/circles/arcs], radius | diameter: expr, near: [x,y] (which of the solutions). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: 3-Tangent Circle
params: curves: [three lines/circles/arcs], near: [x,y] (which of the solutions). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Center Point Slot
params: center: slot centre, end: one arc centre, width: number or expression (an expression naming a parameter is a dimension driven by it); returns centre_line and middle. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Three Point Arc Slot
params: start, through, end: points on the centre arc, width: number or expression (an expression naming a parameter is a dimension driven by it); returns centre_arc and middle. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Center Point Arc Slot
params: center, start: centre arc start, end: direction of the centre arc end (counter-clockwise) or sweep: degrees (0 < sweep < 360), width: number or expression (an expression naming a parameter is a dimension driven by it); returns centre_arc and middle. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Ellipse
params: center, major: end of the major axis [x,y] (a coordinate of either may be an expression over the design's parameters: the point follows them), minor: a point the ellipse passes through on the minor side [x,y] | minor_radius: number or expression (an expression naming a parameter is a dimension driven by it). Also adds its major and minor axes as construction lines through the centre (their ends: the major end and the point opposite it, and the two ends of the minor axis on the ellipse), held by midpoint, perpendicular and point-on-curve constraints, so a half-axis is the distance from the centre to an axis end and an axis line's length is a full axis; axes?: bool (default true; false: the ellipse alone, as the Ellipse tool draws it with Draw ellipses with their axes off). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Fit Point Spline
params: points: [[x,y] or point refs…] (2…500): the spline passes through them; each fit point has an editable tangent handle whose direction and length control curvature, periodic?: boolean (default false); periodic cubic fit closes smoothly through at least 3 distinct samples. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Control Point Spline
params: points: control points (2…500), cubic. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Control Point Spline (Degree 5)
params: points: control points (2…500), degree 5. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Add Spline Point
params: curve: fit point spline id, at: [x,y]: a fit point is inserted where the curve passes nearest to it, between its neighbours (the curve still runs through it and all its old points; constraints on them stay); end?: start|end: `at` becomes the spline's new first or last point instead, and the curve runs on to it (refused when that end is joined to other geometry). Control point splines take no new points yet. Returns point: the new point's id

label: Remove Spline Point
params: curve: spline id, point: one of its points (a point id, or the curve's start or end such as s1.end): the spline runs through (or over) its other points only, and the point goes with the constraints on it unless another curve uses it. Fit point, control point and closed splines. Refused for a closed spline's closing point, for an end joined to other geometry or held by a constraint, when fewer than 2 points would be left (3 on a closed spline), and for a projected, offset or patterned spline. Returns curve, point: the point's id, deleted: whether the point went too

label: Add Tangent Handles
params: curve: fit point spline id: gives it a tangent handle at each fit point (a free point joined to it by a construction line) where the curve already runs, so its shape does not change until a handle is moved; moving a fit point moves the handles nobody has turned with it. In the app a selected spline shows its handles and the first drag of one adds them. Refused for a spline that has handles already, a control point, projected, offset, patterned or equation spline. Returns curve, handles: the handle point ids in fit point order

label: Reset Tangent Handles
params: curve: fit point spline id: removes its tangent handles (the handle points, their construction lines and the constraints on them), so the curve runs through its fit points as if the handles had never been moved; selected, it shows them again where they start. Refused for a spline without tangent handles. Returns curve, removed: the removed handle point ids in fit point order

label: Reverse Spline Direction

The variable is a plain number: sin(t) reads it in radians; a result without a unit is in the design's length unit. With variable_unit "range" it is a length, so a ^ 2 / (4 * t) is a length when a is one: start and end must both be lengths, or one a length and the other a plain number, which is then in the design's unit. Makes a fit point spline through fixed points, as many as the tolerance needs (up to 500), closed smoothly when it ends where it starts; the points are placed again from the formulas whenever the parameters change. Returns curve, points (how many), closed, deviation (mm). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: 3D Spline
params: points: [[x,y,z]…] world fit points (2 or more, coordinates numbers or expressions as for sketch.line3d): a smooth 3D curve through them (needs 3D Sketch on). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: 3D Arc
params: start, through, end: [x,y,z] world points (coordinates numbers or expressions as for sketch.line3d): an exact circular arc through them, from start through through to end (needs 3D Sketch on). Stored exactly (centre, radius, angles), so path consumers can treat it as a true arc. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: 3D Point
params: point: [x,y,z] world point, coordinates numbers or expressions as for sketch.line3d (needs 3D Sketch on). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Move 3D Point
params: wire: drawn 3D curve or point id, index?: fit point (default 0) | point: a point on the sketch plane (`l1.end`, `p3`: a line's end, a fit point of a spline, a lone point; needs 3D Sketch on); to: [x,y,z] | by: [dx,dy,dz] (world); points joined to it move too, and the sketch's 3D constraints are solved with the moved point held where it was put (refused when they cannot hold it there, or when it is fixed). A `point` on the plane first turns the lines and fit-point splines through it (or the lone point) into drawn 3D curves through the same places, which `curves` lists (`wire` and `index` say where the point is now); their constraints and dimensions go. Arcs, circles, ellipses, conics and control-point or closed splines through it are refused

label: Along Axis
params: line: a drawn 3D line's id | lines: [ids]; axis: x|y|z (the axes of the sketch's 3D space: its component's, for a sketch in a component); sketch?: id|name. Holds each line parallel to the axis; refused when that conflicts with the sketch's other 3D constraints. Returns one constraint id per line

label: On Plane
params: point: a 3D point ref (`w1.start`, `.end`, `.through`, `.<n>`, or a 3D point's id) | points: [refs]; plane: xy|yz|xz (the origin planes of the sketch's 3D space); sketch?: id|name. Holds each point on the plane; refused when that conflicts with the sketch's other 3D constraints. Returns one constraint id per point

label: Zebra Analysis
params: stripes?: number across the view (default 12); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: Draft Analysis
params: pull?: [x,y,z] direction (default Z); angle?: degrees (default 1); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: Environment Map Analysis
params: clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: Accessibility Analysis
params: direction?: [x,y,z] the tool comes from (default Z, from above); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: Curvature Map Analysis
params: radius?: mm shown red (default: a tenth of the model's size); clear?: true turns the analysis off

label: View Analysis
params: off?: true turns the view analysis on now off. → active: the command id of the view analysis on (inspect.zebra, inspect.draft, inspect.curvature_map, inspect.environment_map, inspect.accessibility, inspect.continuity, inspect.isocurve or inspect.curvature_comb), or null. One is on at a time: turning one on turns the one on before off. Read-only without `off`

label: Continuity Analysis
params: body?: name (default: the visible bodies); edges?: [x,y,z] points or {"index": i} (default: every edge of the body; a pick must match one body); samples?: 3…257 stations along each edge, ends included (default 33); gap_tolerance_mm? (default 0.001), angle_tolerance_deg? (default 1), curvature_tolerance_per_mm? (default 0.01), curvature_change_tolerance_per_mm2? (default 0.001), curvature_change_rate_tolerance_per_mm3? (default 0.0001); add?: true keeps the seams already shaded and adds these (measuring an edge again replaces it); clear?: true turns the analysis off. → each edge's worst gap (G0), normal angle (G1), curvature jump (G2), jump of the curvature's change across the seam dκ/ds (G3) and of that change's rate d²κ/ds² (G4), from the faces' exact derivatives, as {value, at: [x,y,z], edge_fraction}; its order (g0…g4: the highest every station meets within the tolerances, null where the faces do not meet), its verdict (smooth: g2 or better, curvature_jump, sharp or gap) and a summary; the seams are shaded in the viewport

label: Boundary Surface
params: Either a loop of one sketch's curves — sketch?: id|name (default: the sketch being edited); curves: [2 to 4 sketch curve ids in loop order] (each one ends where the next begins and the last where the first does; two: the patch spans between them and leaves each boundary along the tangent across it; three or four: the flat patch of the loop, three collapsing the side opposite the first curve to the corner there); continuity?: g0|g1|g2|g3 | [one per curve] (default g1: how much of the surface across each boundary the patch repeats — a sketch curve's own plane, so g1 and up hold exactly and g0 lets the middle bow); crown?: number -0.9…3 (default 0: how full the middle is, without touching a boundary; two curves only); samples?: 8…512 stations per boundary (default 25) — or a curve network — u: [curve] (two or more one way: the surface lofts through them), v?: [curve] (crossing every u-curve once: two each way give a Coons patch, more a Gordon surface through every curve; a curve that misses another by more than 0.01 mm is refused, naming the pair), each curve "id" (a curve of `sketch`) | {sketch?: id|name, curves: [ids meeting end to end]} (planar or 3D sketch curves) | {body: name, edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on a chain of its edges), continuity?: g0|g1|g2 (default g0; g1 the surface leaves tangent to the face beside a surface's open edges, g2 with its curvature too; on curves of one direction only)} | {point: [x,y,z]} (a side collapsed to a point: a three-sided patch); operation?: new|join (default new; join sews the surface into the body of its first edge curve, a solid when it closes the gap). name?, body_name? (a surface body)

label: Patch
params: sketch?: id|name and profiles? (planar patches of sketch regions) or profiles_3d: [indices] (the sketch's planar 3D-sketch loops, each patched in its own plane, as listed by sketch.inspect) | edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on a closed loop of a body's edges: one face on them, planar when the loop is, else a smooth B-spline surface) and body?; continuity?: g0|g1|g2|g3|g4 (edges only, default g0: how the patch meets the faces beside the loop — g1 their tangent planes, g2 also their curvature across the edges, g3 also its rate of change, g4 the change of that rate) or [{edge: [x,y,z], g: g0|g1|g2|g3|g4}] (those edges so, the rest g0) or {all, edges}; points?: [[x,y,z]] (edges only, up to 64: points the patch passes through); crown?: number −0.9…3 (default 0: only a fitted patch, whose middle becomes fuller by this many times the loop's size — the bump vanishes on the loop, so the face still meets the picked edges and the continuity across them; a loop that is planar and g0 is the exact plane whatever the crown; with points, crown needs a g1 or higher edge); name?, body_name?

label: Stitch
params: bodies: [names] (surfaces sewn into the first; a solid when they close); tolerance?: expr (default: tight)

label: Thicken
params: bodies: [surface names]; thickness: expr (negative: against the normal); symmetric?: bool; operation?: new|join|cut|intersect; targets?

label: Extend
params: body: surface name; edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on boundary edges to push out); distance: expr (unless up_to); mode?: natural (the surface itself continued: a B-spline's end spans continued, which keeps planes and surfaces of revolution on themselves; the default) | tangent (the face continued tangent to its surface across the edge, G1) | curvature (continued keeping the surface's curvature across the edge too, G2); up_to?: plane (XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal}) | {body, point} (a face, its surface extended) | "bounds" (natural: back to the surface's own bounds, undoing a trim); neighbours?: bool (default true: the edges next to an extended edge are lengthened to meet it; false: the extension's sides run square to the edge)

label: Trim
params: body: surface name; plane: XY|XZ|YZ|plane name|{origin, normal} or tool: {body, point} (a face, its surface extended) or curves: {sketch, curves?: [curve ids] (chains of curves meeting end to end; default every curve), direction?: normal|[x,y,z] (swept onto the surface along the sketch's normal, the default, or this direction)}; keep: [x,y,z] (a point on the side to keep) or [[x,y,z], ...] (points on the regions to keep: the pieces that hang together once cut). Mutual trim: with: another surface (one face each; leave out plane, tool and curves), keep_with: [x,y,z] or [[x,y,z], ...] (what to keep of it); each is cut where the other's surface (extended) meets it; extend?: bool (a surface that stops short of the other is extended to meet it); stitch?: bool (the kept pieces sewn into `body`; `with` is then gone)

label: Surface Extrude
params: sketch?: id|name; curves?: [curve ids] (open or closed chains of curves meeting end to end) and/or profiles? (their boundaries; the default when no curves are given); distance: expr; direction?: positive|negative|symmetric (symmetric: distance is the total, split evenly around the start plane, as solid.extrude); convention?: total_distance|legacy_per_side (as solid.extrude; default total_distance; legacy_per_side: the distance on each side, as older symmetric surface extrudes keep); distance2?: expr; start_offset?: expr; name?, body_name? (a surface body: walls only, no caps)

label: Surface Revolve
params: sketch?: id|name; curves?: [curve ids] and/or profiles? (as surface.extrude); axis: sketch line id|x|y|X|Y|Z|{type: world, axis: X|Y|Z}|{sketch, curve} (a line of another sketch, followed in that sketch)|construction axis name|{origin, dir} (origin: numbers or length expressions, followed when parameters change) | {edge|face: [x,y,z]} (a straight or circular edge, or a cylinder, cone or torus face: about its axis, followed as the model changes); angle?: expr (default 360 deg); angle2?: expr (the other side); symmetric?: bool; name?, body_name? (a surface body, no caps; a solid where a full turn closes it)

label: Surface Sweep
params: sketch?: id|name; curves?: [curve ids] and/or profiles? (as surface.extrude); path_sketch: sketch; path: [curve ids in order] (a path with corners, or 3D curves, gives ruled walls mitred at the corners); path_body?: body name; path_edges?: [points on its edges] (the path is a chain of that body's edges, instead of a sketch's curves); orientation?, twist?, scale?, rails?, rail_fit? (as solid.sweep); name?, body_name? (a surface body, no caps)

label: Surface Loft
params: sections: [{sketch, curves?: [curve ids], profiles?} | {body, edges: [[x,y,z]]}] (2…50 in order; each one chain: a profile without holes, or curves meeting end to end, planar or of a 3D sketch; all open or all closed (all open with a 3D sketch curve); a body edge chain takes the face the chain bounds as the surface the end repeats); continuity?: [g0|g1|g2|g3, g0|g1|g2|g3] (each end, default g0: how much of the surface at the first and last section the loft repeats — the tangent plane, the curvature, or how that curvature changes); crown?: [number, number] (default 0: how full each end leaves, -0.9 flattest to 3 fullest); rails?, rail_fit? (as solid.loft; planar sketch sections only, both ends g0); name?, body_name? (a surface body: ruled between two sections, smooth through three or more; no caps)

label: Offset Surface
params: faces: [[x,y,z]] (points on the faces); body?; distance: expr (signed, along the faces' normals; 0 copies the faces); chain?: bool (each pick's whole smooth chain of faces); tolerance?: expr (how far a fitted face may stray, default 0.01 mm). Planes and cylinders move exactly; other faces are fitted. A new surface body (a solid where its faces close)

label: Ruled Surface
params: body; edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on a chain of its edges, open or closed); distance: expr (how far the strip reaches); mode?: normal|tangent|angle|direction (default normal: along the normal of the face beside each edge; tangent: continuing it); angle?: expr (angle mode: from `direction`, else from the face's normal, turned away from the face; 90 deg from the normal is tangent); direction?: [x,y,z] (direction mode: the rulings; angle mode: the reference, e.g. a pull direction for a draft); face?: [x,y,z] (a point on the face the directions come from; default: the face beside the most picked edges); flip?: bool (the other side); corners?: mitre|round (sharp corners of the chain; inside corners are always cut back); far?: [null|[[x,y,z]]] (per chain edge, the interior control points of a free strip's far curve, as the default curve's handles list them; null: the default). A constant ruling, or one keeping its angle to an arc's axis, gives an exact plane, cylinder or cone; where the rulings turn freely along an edge, the strip is the exact ruled surface to a far curve of its own (from corner to corner, fair, near the rulings' ends). A new surface body

label: Blend Surface
params: from, to: {body, edges: [[x,y,z]]} (points on the edges of one chain of each body: two picks on the same edge is that one edge, more chain up); continuity?: [g0|g1|g2|g3, g0|g1|g2|g3] (each end, default g1: how much of the surface at the picked edges the blend repeats — the tangent plane, the curvature, or how that curvature changes); bulge?: [number, number] (default 0: how full each end leaves, -0.9 flattest to 3 fullest); align?: [[x,y,z], [x,y,z]] (a point each end leaves towards, when the faces at the picks do not say); seam?: [[x,y,z], [x,y,z]] (a point on each chain its stations start from: two closed chains otherwise pair the way that keeps the blend from twisting; an open chain starts at the end nearer its point; a closed chain blends only to a closed chain); stitch?: bool (sew the blend onto its two bodies where the boundaries meet, replacing them); name?, body_name?

label: Untrim
params: face: {body, point}; holes?: all|[[x,y,z]] (points on the inner loops to remove; default: all); outer?: bool (restore the outer boundary to the surface's natural bounds: a free-form surface's own, an analytic surface's span of the face); in_place?: bool (untrim a surface body's face where it is; a solid's face is always copied out). A surface body; the face keeps its name

label: Unstitch
params: body; faces?: [[x,y,z]] (points on the faces to take out, each its own surface body; the rest stay together under the body's name; default: every face its own surface body). A solid comes apart into surfaces

label: Reverse Normal
params: body (a surface); faces?: [[x,y,z]] (points on the faces to turn over; default: all of them)

label: Fair Surface
params: body: surface name; faces?: [[x,y,z]] points on the faces to fair (default: every face); strength?: number (0..1 of the full fairing step, default 1); iterations?: number (1..1000 steps, default 1); keep_edges?: bool (default true: hold the boundary row and the row next to it, so a face keeps meeting its neighbours in position and in tangent); tolerance?: expr mm (how far a control vertex may move, default 0.001 of the body's size). Moves the interior control vertices of each B-spline face to flatten its curvature variation while the boundary stays put: the face keeps its edges and the body its shape within the tolerance, and the warning in the reply carries the energy before and after; name?

label: Surface Fillet
params: planned: a, b: {body, point} (two faces of separate bodies that meet or cross; the points pick the side the ball rolls on); radius: expr; trim?: both|first|none

label: Match Surface
params: body: surface name (the body whose face is rebuilt); faces?: [[x,y,z]] (points on that face, default: the body's first); target: body name (the body the seam must meet); edges: [[x,y,z]] (points on one edge chain of the target: the rebuilt boundary takes its place); order?: g1|g2|g3 (default g2: position and tangent plane, the curvature too, or how that curvature changes along the seam). The far boundary stays where it was and the body keeps its name

label: Fillet
params: point: corner shared by two curves ("l1.end") | points: [corners] (all rounded alike: one radius, the rest equal; a corner is a point reference or {a, b}, the two curves meeting there) | a, b: two lines or arcs meeting at a corner (two lines that share no end are first brought to where they meet: the nearer end of a line that stops short moves there, and a line that runs past is cut there, losing its shorter piece); radius: expr. A corner that dimensions or constraints measure to stays as a virtual sharp corner on both curves' extensions (`virtual_corners`; the moved ones in `moved_to_virtual_corner`). An ellipse's axis line is never a side of a corner (also for the chamfers). A corner of an offset's lines and arcs first releases that offset (also for the chamfers): its curves keep following their sources at the offset's distance, held by dimensions that keep its parameter (`offset_released`: curve ids). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Equal Distance Chamfer
params: point | points: [corners] (every corner cut alike; a corner is a point reference or {a, b}) | a, b: a corner of two lines (two that share no end are first brought to where they meet, as in sketch.fillet); distance. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Distance and Angle Chamfer
params: point | points: [corners] (every corner cut alike; a corner is a point reference or {a, b}, and a point's `a` is the first of its two lines in curve order) | a, b: a corner of two lines (two that share no end are first brought to where they meet, as in sketch.fillet); distance: along a, angle: deg from a. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Two Distance Chamfer
params: point | points: [corners] (every corner cut alike; a corner is a point reference or {a, b}, and a point's `a` is the first of its two lines in curve order) | a, b: a corner of two lines (two that share no end are first brought to where they meet, as in sketch.fillet); distance: along a, distance2: along b. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Offset
params: curves: [ids], distance: number in mm or length expression (creates an editable dimension; positive = left of the chain, or toward `side`), side?: [x,y], chain?: bool (default true: the connected chain, including ends that only coincide). A corner is trimmed back to the crossing when the offset runs past it, and extended until the offset curves intersect when the corner falls short; direction?: one_side|symmetric (default one_side) or symmetric?: bool (the same distance each way; no `side`, whose job it takes over), distance2?: positive length expression (Two Sides: an independent distance the other way, as for `solid.extrude`). Each side is its own offset association, listed in `sides`; flip?: bool reverses the primary side; `param`/`param2` name the driving dimensions; instances?: whole number or unitless expression, 1…100 (default 1): each instance after the first offsets the instance before it by the same distance again, so instance n stands n distances from the curves picked. Every instance of a side is driven by that side's own dimension, and each entry of `sides` names its `instance`; an instance the shape cannot take refuses the whole command. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Break Offset Association
params: curve: derived offset curve id (retains geometry and makes its points editable)

label: Trim
params: curve: id, at: [x,y] (the piece to remove: between the nearest intersections around it). Trimming a line, circle or arc that has offsets, or a piece of an offset's copy (from one curve, or from several lines and arcs), releases the offset first (offset_released: curve ids): each copy keeps following its source at the offset's distance, held by dimensions that keep the offset's parameter. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Trim Along Path
params: points: [[x,y]…] (2…2000 positions: a path drawn across the sketch). Every piece the path crosses is removed as `sketch.trim` removes the piece at that crossing, in the order the path crosses them; a piece crossed again after it is gone is not trimmed twice; offset copies are trimmed as `sketch.trim` trims them, keeping their distance; projected geometry, infinite lines, offset copies trim can't release and pieces trim refuses are passed over (why in `skipped`). dry_run?: bool (report without changing the design). One undo step → trimmed: [each trim's result], removed: [[[x,y]…]] (each removed piece as a polyline). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Extend
params: curve: id, at: [x,y] near the end to extend (a line runs on to the nearest curve, or the previewed reach when nothing is in the way; an arc grows along its circle and closes into a whole circle when nothing stops it) | curves: [id, id] (two lines or arcs of this sketch, grown until they meet and joined there), at?: [[x,y],[x,y]] (one point per curve: the end to grow; default the end nearest the meeting point). `curve` and `curves` exclude each other; the two-curve form returns moved: the meeting point's id

label: Break
params: curve: id, at: [x,y] (split at intersections; at a point where the curve ends and another curve meets, the curve gets its own end there and the two are no longer joined) | points: [[x,y]…] (1…1000 positions projected onto the curve; duplicates are merged). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Sketch Scale
params: entities: [curve/point ids], base: [x,y] or point ref, factor: number; the driving length and radius dimensions wholly inside the selection scale too (a formula becomes `(formula) * factor`)

label: Transform
params: entities: [curve/point ids], factor?: number (scale), angle?: degrees (turn), center?: [x,y] or point ref (what scales and turns stay put; default [0,0]), translate?: [dx,dy] (applied last); scales, turns and moves in one step

label: Move/Copy Sketch Entities
params: entities: [ids], translate?: [dx,dy], angle?: deg, center?: [x,y], copy?: bool, rotate_constraints?: bool (default true; false keeps constraints unchanged); a rotation turns the constraints tied to the sketch axes when all their geometry moves (horizontal and vertical relations and dimensions swap at odd quarter turns and stay at half turns, line angles turn with the line) and removes the horizontal and vertical ones that cannot hold at other angles; picking a text outline or linked point transforms its whole text source once, and copies remain editable text; copy also accepts drawn 3D curves, preserving exact arcs and height above the sketch plane; a turned rectangle keeps its shape: parallel and perpendicular relations replace the horizontal and vertical ones lost; returns `released`: the constraints tying the moved geometry to what stays that the move let go, as {id, kind}, and `added`: the relations put in their place, as {id, kind}. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Mirror
params: entities: [curve/point ids], line: straight curve id, x / y for a sketch axis, or {axis: X|Y|Z} for an origin axis (the mirror line is the axis's projection into the sketch plane; an axis perpendicular to the plane is refused) (symmetry constraints are added). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Circular Pattern
params: entities: [ids], center: [x,y] or point ref, count: 2…500 (number or unitless expression, retained through edits), angle?: total deg, number or expression (default 360); alignment?: left|center|right (default right); reversed?: bool (default false). Quantity includes the original. Center balances copies around it; reversed flips the direction and extra side for even totals. Partial arcs span angle with angle/(count-1) spacing; full turns use angle/count. Adds associative pattern constraints; a coordinate center creates a constrainable point. Returns pattern and center ids. pattern?: existing pattern id to edit (omitted values retained; surviving instance ids retained). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Rectangular Pattern
params: entities: [ids], count, spacing; count2?, spacing2?; counts: positive integer numbers or expressions, at most 500 instances total; spacings: length numbers or expressions; direction?, direction2?: sketch line ids (live references); dir?, dir2?: [x,y] vectors (defaults: sketch x, perpendicular to direction 1); alignment?, alignment2?: left|center|right (default right). Signed spacings reverse each direction. reversed?, reversed2?: bool (default false); reverses placement and the extra side of even centered totals. Quantities include the original. Adds associative pattern constraints. Returns pattern id. pattern?: existing pattern id to edit (omitted values retained; surviving instance ids retained). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Project
params: refs: [{edge: [x,y,z], body?} | {face: [x,y,z], body?} (its edge loops) | {body: name} (silhouette) | {vertex: [x,y,z], body?} | {sketch, curve} | {sketch, point} | {point: name} (a construction point) | "origin" | {axis: X|Y|Z|name} | {plane: XY|XZ|YZ|name}]; projection_link?: bool (default true); construction?: bool (default the session's preference, off: the created curves are construction geometry). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Intersect
params: refs: [{body}, {face: [x,y,z], body?}, {edge: [x,y,z], body?}, {sketch, curve}]: section curves (or points) with the sketch plane; projection_link?: bool (default true); construction?: bool (default the session's preference, off: the created curves are construction geometry). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Include 3D Geometry
params: refs: like Project (edges, vertices, sketch curves and points); curves out of the sketch plane are flattened onto it; construction?: bool (default the session's preference, off: the created curves are construction geometry). Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Project To Surface
params: curves: [{sketch, curve}…] (curves of other sketches), face: [x,y,z] point on the target face, body?: projected along the active sketch's normal onto the face, as linked 3D curves. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Intersection Curve
params: a, b: {body} | {face: [x,y,z], body?} | {sketch, curve} (a curve of another sketch, standing in for its extrusion along that sketch's normal): where they meet, as linked 3D curves. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Spun Profile
params: body: name, axis: a line of the active sketch (curve id) | X|Y|Z: the body's outline revolved about the axis, in the sketch plane. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Isoparametric Curve
params: face: [x,y,z] point on the face (the curve passes through it), body?, direction?: u|v|[x,y,z] (default u): linked 3D curve. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: Fit Curves to Mesh Section
params: body: name (a mesh or solid body): its section with the sketch plane, fitted with lines and arcs, as normal (unlinked) geometry. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

starts?: 1..8 (lead = starts x pitch: that many grooves, each a turn's starts-th further round; a designation that gives the lead gives the starts); ease_out?: expr|standard|short (modelled threads: the inner end, away from where the thread starts, fades out over this length (shorter than a turn too), its section moving out of the material as it turns; standard 2.5 P, short 1.25 P per ISO 3508; it lies past the full-form length, up to a shoulder's clearance; at a free end, inside the face; without it the groove stops square there, ending in its own profile; the start never fades: it runs off its free end, plain or chamfered (`tip`)); tip?: none|start|both (modelled external threads: start chamfers the end the thread starts from, which must be free, both each free end the thread reaches, ISO 4753's chamfered end, the last teeth tapering into the cone; chamfer_angle?: angle expr to the axis, default 45 deg; chamfer_depth?: expr, radial from the major diameter, default for a metric thread down to the external minor diameter d3 = d - 1.226869 P (ISO 724), the largest ISO 4753 allows; modeled?: bool (default false); continuous_flanks?: bool (default true; false keeps the historical half-turn faces and groove-before-chamfer construction). label: Flange
params: base: sketch + profiles? (rule?, flip?) | contour: sketch + curves (open chain of lines and tangent arcs) + distance (rule?, flip?, reverse?) | edge: edges: [[x,y,z] on top/bottom edges, or {point: [x,y,z], angle?, height?, segments?} for an edge with its own angle and height, or split into 1…64 segments [{from, to, angle?, height?, flip?}] that tile the stretch the sheet still has there (from, to are fractions 0…1 of it, first from 0, last to 1; consecutive segments that match make one bend)] + height (along the flange, to its far edge), angle? (default 90 deg), radius? (default: rule), height_from?: outer|inner|tangent (where the height is measured from: the outer virtual sharp (default), the inner virtual sharp, or past 90 deg the line square to the flange touching the bend's outside (tangent; up to 90 deg the outer sharp)), position?: inside|outside|middle|material_outside|tangent (where the bend starts: the outer virtual sharp on the edge (default), the bend starting at the edge (bend_outside is the same), half way, the inner virtual sharp on the edge, or the bend's outer face tangent to the edge's face (below 90 deg the bend's end on that face)), flip?, body?, corner_relief_shape?: notch|round|rectangular|tear and corner_relief? (size across): the relief at the corners these flanges make (default: the rule's); then?: [{angle?, height, flip?}] further bends (at most 16), each a flange on the far edge of the one before, flip: true turns that bend the other way (edge only); type?: base|edge|contour (default from the inputs); name?, body_name? (the new body). Thickness, K-factor and bend radius come from the rule (sheet.manage_rules); passing them here is refused, and so is the corner relief on a base or contour flange

label: Path Flange
params: edge: [x,y,z] on a top or bottom edge of the sheet; sketch + curves: an open chain of sketch lines drawn on a plane across that edge, from the edge out (each line one flange as long as the line, to the outer face from the virtual sharp; each corner one bend, turning the way the lines turn); radius? label: Sheet Metal Rules
params: name (new or existing); thickness?, k_factor?, bend_radius?, relief_width?, relief_depth?, corner_relief?, hem_gap?, gap? label: List Sheet Metal Rules
params: → rules with their expressions and values, and the active one

label: Create Flat Pattern
params: body? → flat size, outline loops and cut-outs (flat coordinates, as point lists), cutout_shapes (the same cut-outs exactly, in the same order: {circle: {center, radius}} for a round hole, else {segments: [{line: [a, b]} | {arc: {center, radius, start_deg, sweep_deg}} | {polyline: [...]}]}), pockets (with their own cutout_shapes), bend lines and the bend table

label: Export Flat Pattern as DXF
params: body?, path?, curves?: exact|arcs (default exact: an ellipse as ELLIPSE, splines, text outlines and other Béziers as SPLINE; arcs: tangent arcs and lines within 0.001 mm, for machines that read only those), text?: cut|etch (default cut: letters that text cut through the sheet are cut contours on layer TEXT; etch: single contours on layer ETCH and the sheet keeps its material there; text machined to a depth is always on ETCH), bend_notes?: bool (default false: a note beside each bend line on layer BEND_NOTES, `B1 UP 90° R1`, its angle the included angle when the body's rule has angle_display: included), note_height?: mm (default 3), bend_lines?: bool (default true; false leaves BEND_UP and BEND_DOWN out, for a cutter that would cut them), layers?: roles|single (default roles, the layers below; single: every entity on layer 0), per_body?: bool (a file for every sheet body, `<path>-<body>.dxf`, or their DXF texts without a path → files: [{body, path | dxf, bends}]; not with `body`) → DXF (AutoCAD 2000, mm): layers OUTLINE (the outer contour), CUT (what is cut out inside it), TEXT or ETCH (letters), BEND_UP and BEND_DOWN (dashed centre lines), BEND_NOTES, POCKET_<BOTTOM|TOP|INTERNAL>_Z<from>_TO_<to>_MM (one per side and depth) and PERFORATION; inner contours come before the outline

params: sketch: the frame sketch (id or name; 2D or 3D); lines?: [curve ids] (one member each; default: every straight line drawn in the sketch: not construction, not projected or otherwise linked, not of no length); profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions} | profile_sketch: a sketch whose profile is the section, in its own x and y around its origin, with profiles?: picks as solid.extrude takes them (default: its material, nested loops alternating, so two circles make a tube); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point that sits on each line, default origin); locate?: [x,y] (the profile point that sits on each line, in mm from the profile's own origin: a bar's or an angle's bottom-left corner, a channel's web back at mid-height, the centre of other profiles; takes precedence over `anchor` and keeps the member attached at that point when the profile size changes); angle?: angle expr (the profile turned about the line; default 0: its y as near world up as the line allows, a vertical member's x along world X); mirror?: bool (the profile mirrored across its y axis); name?; body_name? params: family?: RSC|PFC|RSA|SHS|RHS|CHS (list only that family's sizes). Returns kinds: [{kind, label, required, optional, example}]: the built-in profiles, each SolidCraft's own parametric definition; and sizes: [{family, kind, standard, source, names, additional?}]: the standard steel sizes by name, each family with the published table its dimensions come from (frame.profile.properties with {profile: {size}} gives a size's dimensions and section)

label: Insert Profile
params: profile: {kind: bar|round_bar|rect_tube|round_tube|angle|channel|i_beam, …its dimensions: each a number in the design's units or a length expression over its parameters ("tube_wall", "2 in"); a channel's flange_slope is an angle (a number of degrees)} (frame.profile.list gives each kind's dimensions and an example; dimensions left out take defaults from the profile's size) | {size: a standard steel size by name, such as "RSC 203x89", "PFC 200x90x30", "RSA 50x50x5", "SHS 100x100x5", "RHS 200x100x6.3" or "CHS 42.4x3.2" (frame.profile.list lists them), alone: it brings its dimensions}; at?: [x,y] (sketch mm, default the origin); anchor?: origin|center|centroid|top_left|top|top_right|left|right|bottom_left|bottom|bottom_right (the profile point placed on `at`: its origin, the default and a built-in profile's centre, its bounding box's centre, its centroid, or a corner or edge middle of its bounding box); angle?: radians, counter-clockwise; fixed?: bool (default true: the curves are locked, so solving the sketch keeps the shape); sketch?: id|name (default: the sketch being edited). Returns the section as frame.profile.properties does. Returns created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what it added (stable and never reused: usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.*, sketch.delete…)

label: End Cap
params: faces: [{face:[x,y,z],body,index,path?}] planar end faces of frame members, picked in world mm (1–256); thickness: length in design units or a parameter expression; offset?: inset of the plate from the outside of the profile, a length; ratio?: the inset as a share of the thickness (give offset or ratio, not both; neither: the plate is flush with the outside of the profile); chamfer?: corner chamfer length along each edge from the corner (default 0; a rounded corner needs at least its rounding); direction?: outward|inward (default outward: past the end; inward: the member is cut back by the thickness and the cap takes its place). Common name/body_names fields supported.

label: Cycle Component Color

params: name?, parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); parent_path?: exact parent placement; activate?: bool (default true); grounded?: bool (default: true for the design's first part, false otherwise)

label: Create Components from Bodies
params: bodies: [names] → one new component per body, named after it

label: Activate Component
params: component: id or name (0 or "root" for the design); occurrence?, path?: exact placement used to author shared geometry

label: Edit in Place
params: component: id or name of a linked component; path?: its placement (occurrence ids, default its first) → in the app window: open the design it links in a tab of its own with the assembly drawn around it (component.finish_edit goes back); fails when it is not linked, the assembly has no file yet, something is open or running in it, or the file is missing, on a network location not allowed yet or open in another SolidCraft; asked during the agent's turn it opens once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere it only checks

label: Finish Edit
params: no parameters → in the app window: go back from the linked design edited in place to its assembly, which reads it again; fails while the design has unsaved changes (run file.save first) or something is open in it; asked during the agent's turn it finishes once the turn ends (queued: true); elsewhere nothing changes

label: List Components
params: compact?: bool (counts of bodies, features, sketches and construction planes instead of their names; occurrences leave out identity transforms; children as occurrence ids); bodies?: bool (with compact: body names, not their count)

params: component?: id or name (default active); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Measures the first placement, or all placements for root, including pending moves; material-aware mass and center of mass in world coordinates; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 (the inertia tensor about the body's center of mass, world axes, from its tessellation) only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total.first_moment_g_mm (mass × center of mass), inertia_g_mm2 about the total center of mass, principal_moments_g_mm2 (smallest first) and principal_axes (unit, right-handed); with about, total.inertia_about {point, inertia_g_mm2}

label: Occurrence Physical Properties
params: occurrence: id or name; path?: [occurrence ids] (required if nested under multiple instances); descendants?: bool (default true); about?: [x, y, z] (mm). Physical properties of this placement in world coordinates, including pending moves; volume, density, mass, center of mass and inertia_g_mm2 only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; total.open_bodies_skipped counts open bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; total inertia as in component.properties

label: Rename Component
params: component, name

label: Delete Component
params: component: deletes it, its subcomponents, occurrences and features

label: Unlock Contents
params: component: removes the rigid joints that hold its contents together (an imported assembly's rigid group), so its parts move and take joints one by one → joints (the ids removed)

label: Move Bodies to Component
params: bodies: [names], component; component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance); from_path?: the placement of their component they move from (default: its only one, else its first, where its bodies have their own names)

label: Paste Bodies
params: bodies: [names, as the Browser shows them: a body seen in another placement of its component (`Cube (B:2)`) is copied from there]; component?: where the copies go (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement to place them by (default: its only one, else the active one; a component placed more than once gets them in every instance). params: component?: where it goes (default: the active one); component_path?: its placement (default: the active one, else its only one). Ids, names and timeline order stay; the geometry stays where it is in the world; the bodies the features made move with them. Refused while the timeline is rolled back, for a component placed more than once, and for a move that would break a feature (nothing changes)

label: Move to Component

One undo step, all or nothing: placements move first (taking what they hold), then features (taking the bodies they made), then the bodies still elsewhere (a body transfer, which leaves its features behind)

label: Paste (Instance)
params: component (or occurrence): what to place again; path?: validates selected occurrence; parent?: component (default: the same parent); translate?: [x,y,z]; in_place?: bool (default false: the selected transform within the parent; true: where the selected placement is in the world, translate in world axes; a parent placed more than once is placed by parent_path?, else the active placement, and every instance gets the copy). label: Paste New

label: Sweep Joint
params: joint: id|name; from, to: its value the sweep runs between (degrees for angles, mm for distances, or expressions); index? (which value, default 0); step? (between samples, in the joint's unit; default: fine enough that no part passes through another between two); refine?: mm (the first contact is bisected until no part moves more than this between the last clear value and the touching one; default 0.01); occurrences?: [ids or names] (checked against each other; default every occurrence), with against?: [ids or names] (the parts that stay: each of `occurrences` only against these), or contact_sets?: true (the pairs of the design's contact sets); exclude_pairs?: [[a, b]] (occurrences by id or name: pairs of bodies under a and b are not checked, such as a pin in its hole); budget_s?: seconds (at most 86400; past them the sweep stops with what it found; its work is then not capped. Without it the work caps, 4096 samples, 64 bisection steps and 500 million triangle tests, stop it the same way); report_gaps?: bool (the nearest gap at every sample, default false); apply?: bool (leave the design where the sweep stopped; default false: the design is not changed) → stopped_at (the last value clear of contact, or where a loop or limit stopped it; null: it reached `to`), stopped_by: {a, b, at: [x,y,z] (where they touch, world), a_part, b_part: {component, path: [occurrence names], path_ids} (where each touching body sits)} | "loop" | "limit" | "budget" (stopped_at: the last value checked clear) | null, samples: [{value, min_gap_mm?, pair?, parts?}], min_gap? (report_gaps: {part: {mm, at_value, to}}, the nearest each part came to another), unit, gap_method ("mesh": distances between the tessellations), gap_tolerance_mm (how far those can be off: 0 when every face is flat), pairs (checked), touching_at_start: [[a, b]] (pairs already touching at `from`, such as parts joined face to face or a door on its frame: these stop it only once they pass into each other deeper than they start), touching_parts (where their bodies sit), budget_s, budget_exceeded, budget_ran_out: "time" | "samples" | "bisections" (a contact reported less refined than `refine`) | "intersections" | "work" | null, applied. The parts are tested at the samples and through the bisection; the motion is on a copy (closed loops follow, contact sets do not stop it)

label: Find Joint Limits
params: joint: id|name; index? (one value; default every value); refine?, step?, occurrences?, against?, contact_sets?, exclude_pairs? (as joint.sweep) → values: [{index, dof, unit, value (now), min, max, min_by, max_by, range}], each value swept both ways from where it is, its own limits ignored, closed loops following; each side stops at the first contact (bisected to `refine`), where a loop cannot close, or at another limit (another value's, or another joint's through a motion link): min_by/max_by {a, b, at} | "loop" | "limit" | "budget" (its work ran out: the last value checked clear) | "turn" (an angle with no contact within a turn: a turn from the other side, or ±180° from now when nothing is met at all) | "range" (a distance with no contact within the parts' reach: min/max null); touching_at_start, overlapping_at_start: [{a, b, depth_mm}] (already passing into each other: they stop it only going deeper), refine_mm, gap_method, gap_tolerance_mm, pairs (0: no two parts to check, so nothing is swept).
