label: Compare Parameter Variants
params: variants: [{name, set: {parameter: number | expression}}] (1 to 12; up to 16 existing parameters each). Rebuild each set together in a separate copy of the open design. Returns baseline and ordered results with volume, mass, body counts and rebuild regressions. No edits are kept.

label: New Design
params: name?

label: Open
params: path: .sc design (or a .solidcraft design from an earlier release), .dxf/.svg drawing (opens as a new, unsaved design with an XY sketch, using sketch.insert_dxf/sketch.insert_svg units and defaults), or a .step/.stp/.igs/.fcstd/.3dm/.3mf/.stl/.obj/.glb/.gltf/.kicad_pro/.kicad_pcb file (STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino, 3MF, STL, OBJ, glTF or KiCad PCB; opens as a new design holding the file as a component named after it, as file.insert_step and file.insert_mesh make), or a .ply/.xyz/.pts point cloud (opens as a new design holding it, as pointcloud.insert makes; its `units` and `max_points` as there); up?: z|y for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD, Rhino or glTF file (see file.insert_step and file.insert_mesh); names?: auto|solid|product|instance for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file (see file.insert_step); units?: for an STL or OBJ file (see file.insert_mesh); origin?: bool for a mesh file (see file.insert_mesh); folder?: bool for a STEP, IGES, FreeCAD or Rhino file (see file.insert_step); reuse_import?: bool (STEP/IGES: reuse an unchanged import from the local saved-model cache, default true; false recomputes without reading or writing the cache; → import_reused: bool, content_sha256: exact source digest); history?: features|solids for a FreeCAD file (see file.insert_step); for a KiCad PCB: thickness?: board thickness in mm (default from the board); components?: bool (default true); copper?: "overlay" (default: flat copper just above the board), "none" (leave the traces out) or "mesh" (modelled with thickness; true also means mesh; pads are included whenever copper is enabled); silkscreen?: bool (default true: the silk shapes and text); color?: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (board substrate colour); representation?: mesh|brep (the board itself; default brep: a solid whose faces can be picked); read_only?: bool (a design: saving to its own file is refused, file.save_as keeps the changes elsewhere); verify?: bool (default false: a design's signature is checked and reported, `signature`) → open_elsewhere: {host, user, app, opened} when another SolidCraft has the design open (its lock file is fresh); newer_file: {format, reads_up_to, unknown_changes, not_understood, notice} and warnings when a newer SolidCraft saved it: it opens all the same, and what this version can't read is named there and kept by saving

label: Insert STEP
params: path: STEP, IGES, FreeCAD .FCStd or Rhino .3dm file (its bodies join the design as an Import base feature in a new component named after the file, placed in the active component; an assembly's products become nested components, a repeated part one component with an occurrence per placement, all held as one rigid group until component.unlock → component, component_name, occurrence, subcomponents?, rigid_joints?, group?: the folder); folder?: bool (default false; true: an import that brings more than one item into the history (its Import feature and the rigid joints holding its parts) goes into a new history folder named `Group #N`); flatten?: bool (default false; true: every solid comes in as a body of the import's own component, with no subcomponents, occurrences or joints: a part placed several times is one body per placement where the file places it, and, as no component says which part a body belongs to, its name is prefixed with the outermost named part holding it (`R63: Terminal`), a placeholder name (empty, a bare number, or an exporter's `… STEP translator …`) giving way to its nearest named product's); name? (the feature's and the component's); up?: z|y (default z: the file's axes are kept; y: the file has Y up, so the import's component is turned a quarter turn about X, Y becoming Z → stand_up: its occurrence); names?: auto|solid|product|instance (default auto: keep meaningful solid names, replace placeholders with the nearest named product, else instance; solid: the solid's own name; product: the part's name; instance: the occurrence's name, else the product's); history?: features|solids for a FreeCAD file (default features: its sketches and the Pad, Pocket, Revolution, Groove, Fillet, Chamfer and primitive features that use them are rebuilt as features in the new component, when every one can be and they build what the file holds → features_added, history: "features"; else, or with solids, the file's solids come in as an Import feature, and a warning says why the history was not rebuilt); matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (where the new component's occurrence sits in the active component, after `up`: a rigid row-major 3x4 rotation-and-translation or 4x4 matrix, flat or as rows, as occurrence.move takes it, its translation column (entries 4, 8 and 12) numbers or length expressions: one that names a parameter is kept, and the import follows the parameter when it changes (a grounded one stays); a scale, shear or mirror is refused before the file is read); tolerance? (see occurrence.move)

label: Insert Mesh
params: path: .3mf, .stl, .obj, .ply (with faces), .glb or .gltf file (its meshes join the design as mesh bodies in a new component named after the file → component, component_name, occurrence; a glTF file's node tree becomes nested components held as one rigid group until component.unlock, a mesh placed again another occurrence, its materials the bodies' appearances, and its metres millimetres); name?; up?: z|y for a glTF file (default y: glTF has Y up, so the import's component is turned a quarter turn about X, Y becoming Z → stand_up: its occurrence; z: the file's axes are kept); units?: mm|cm|m|in|ft for an STL or OBJ file, or a PLY file with faces (default mm): the unit its coordinates are in, scaled to millimetres as the file is read (a 3MF or glTF file states its own). The design keeps the millimetre mesh and not the unit, so insert the file again to try another; origin?: bool (default false: the mesh keeps its file's coordinates; true: once read, scaled and stood up, the import's occurrence is moved so the box around its bodies is centred on X and Y of the active component with its lowest point on Z = 0 → moved_to_origin: [x, y, z], the shift made); crease_angle_degrees?: 0..180 (0 clears imported shading normals for the previous flat-shading behavior; positive angles regenerate angle-weighted normals across manifold edges below this crease angle; omitted keeps authored OBJ normals/smoothing groups, or flat shading when absent; geometry stays unchanged)

label: Save
params: path? (default: current file; a name that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (replace the design's file even though another program or computer changed it since it was opened or saved; without it that save is refused); sign?: bool (the app's own Save only: sign the save with GnuPG, appending a provenance record; container only; a script or agent is refused); signing_key?: fingerprint or user id (default: GnuPG's default signing key) → signature: {method, fingerprint, user_id?} when signed

label: Save As
params: path (a design file name, .sc as a rule; one that opens as another kind of file, such as .step, .stl or .dxf, is refused: file.export writes those); format?: container|json (default: json for .json, otherwise container); compression?: fast|compact (default: fast); cache?: bool (the evaluated model, so the design opens without rebuilding; default: true); preview?: bool (saved display meshes, default: false); overwrite?: bool (as file.save, when `path` is the design's own file); sign?: bool and signing_key? (as file.save, and likewise only from the app's own Save)

label: Verify Signature
params: path? (default: the design's current file) → {path, status, reason?, truncated, records: [{method, key_id, user_id?, author?, created?, format, covered}]}: status is unsigned, valid, not_covered (signed earlier, saved since without a key), invalid or unsupported

label: Signing Keys
params: → {available, keys: [{fingerprint, key_id, user_id, on_card}]}: the GnuPG secret keys a save can sign with (desktop only)

label: Recoverable Designs
params: dir? (default: the recovery folder) → designs autosaved by apps that crashed or closed with unsaved changes

label: Recover Design
params: id (from doc.recovery_list); dir?; discard?: bool (delete the entry once open) — opens it with its file path, unsaved

label: Discard Recovered Design
params: id, or all: true; dir?

label: Export
params: path; format?: stl|stla|obj|step|3mf|3mf-tagged|glb|urdf|json (default from extension; 3mf-tagged: 3MF whose triangles carry their B-rep face, at full precision, for meshing and analysis tools; docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md; obj: the colours of the bodies go in a material library (`.mtl`) written next to the mesh file; glb: binary glTF in metres with Y up, each body placed and named, its colours, metallic and roughness as materials; a transparent body or face, or a body a render setup gives an image texture or optics, is refused; urdf: the whole assembly as a robot, with STL meshes written next to it; docs/urdf.md); bodies?: [names] (JSON and URDF export the complete design); urdf only: mesh_prefix? (before each mesh file name, e.g. package://robot/meshes/), effort? (default 1000), velocity? (default 10); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ, 3MF and GLB: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (STL and 3MF only, default false: each body with a print face (body.print_face) is written laid on it, as a slicer export lays it → print_faces: the bodies laid, warnings: each body that has a print face but was written as it lies)

label: Export STEP
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body; a design with components then exports as a STEP assembly) → {path, bytes, format}: STEP, whatever the path's extension

label: Export STL
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body); quality?: standard|fine|finest (default standard); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (default false: as file.export) → {path, bytes, format, print_faces?, warnings?}: binary STL, whatever the path's extension

label: Export 3MF
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body); quality?: standard|fine|finest (default standard); objects?: body|component (as file.export); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (default false: as file.export) → {path, bytes, format, print_faces?, warnings?}: 3MF, whatever the path's extension

label: Export OBJ
params: path; bodies?: [names] (default: every body); quality?: standard|fine|finest (default standard) → {path, bytes, format, files, warnings?}: OBJ, with the colours of the bodies in a material library (`.mtl`) next to it

label: Export URDF
params: path; mesh_prefix?; effort? (default 1000); velocity? (default 10) → {path, format, files, links, joints, warnings}: the whole assembly as a robot, with STL meshes written next to it; docs/urdf.md

label: Save As Mesh
params: path; format?: stl|3mf|3mf-tagged (default from the extension, else stl; 3mf-tagged: docs/formats/3mf-face-tags.md); bodies?: [names] (default: all); ascii?: bool (STL); slicer?: id or name from file.slicers, the program path it lists, or a program the user added under Custom… (send the saved file there, through the same steps as file.send_to_slicer: a slicer that has to be started first is waited for; may be deprecated later in favour of file.send_to_slicer or a Send to App workflow, kept for scripts); single_instance?: bool (default true; see file.send_to_slicer); quality?: standard|fine|finest (STL, OBJ and 3MF: how closely the mesh follows curved faces, a chord tolerance of 2e-4, 5e-5 or 1e-5 of each body's size; default standard); objects?: body|component (3MF only: one object per body, the default, or one object for each placed component with two or more bodies, with those bodies as its parts, so a slicer loads them as one object with parts); lay_on_print_faces?: bool (default false: each body with a print face (body.print_face) is saved laid on it; a file sent to `slicer` is laid on them whatever this says)

label: Send to Slicer
params: slicer: id or name from file.slicers, or a program the user added under Custom…; bodies?: [names] (default: the selected bodies); wait?: block|return|no (default block: a slicer that drops a file at a cold start is started alone and the call waits up to 10 s for it to be ready, then sends; return: start it and answer {starting}; no: send now); single_instance?: bool (default true: PrusaSlicer, SuperSlicer and Cura load the file in the window that is open); format?: 3mf|stl|3mf-tagged (default 3mf, in millimetres; STL if that can't be written) → saves the bodies in this user's slicer folder and opens the file in the slicer. The file name stays the same for the same design and bodies, so sending again replaces it (use the slicer's Reload from disk)

label: Open with EasyPrint
params: consent: bool (required: true only once the user has agreed to upload the model to Printables' servers; it stays there for 30 minutes and opening it needs a Printables sign-in); bodies?: [names] (default: the selected bodies); format?: 3mf|stl (default 3mf, in millimetres) → uploads the bodies to EasyPrint, Printables' slicer in the browser, and opens it in the browser. 100 MB at most. Works in the desktop app and the browser build; the CLI has no way to upload yet

label: Installed Slicers
params: → the slicers found on this machine: [{id, name, program, icon?}]; pass an id, a name or the program path as file.send_to_slicer's or file.save_mesh's `slicer`

label: Clear Reused Imports
params: → removed: number of local cached imports deleted; leaves open designs and remembered stand-up answers unchanged

label: Copy Design File
params: path, destination; copies the saved design without replacing an existing file; rebases linked designs

label: Move Design File
params: path, destination; also renames; refuses the current design or its linked files; never replaces an existing file

label: Move Design File to Trash
params: path; refuses the current design or its linked files; system Trash only, never permanent deletion

label: Insert PCB (Gerber)
params: set?: a board's files as one: a zip, a folder, or any file in the board's folder; each file's layer is found from what it says (Gerber X2, Excellon), the job file (.gbrjob, which also gives thickness and finish) and its name, and outline, drills and layers then name files in the set to use instead; outline: path of the board outline Gerber (RS-274X) layer | outline_text: its text; drills?: path or [paths] of Excellon drill files (up to 16) and/or drills_text?: text or [texts]; thickness?: mm (default 1.6, more than 0, at most 20); name?: the new component's (default: the outline file's name without its extension, or Board); origin?: file (default: keep the files' coordinates) | corner (the lower-left corner of the box around the outline at the origin); layers?: {top_copper?, bottom_copper?, top_mask?, bottom_mask?, top_silk?, bottom_silk?: path of that Gerber layer} and/or layers_text?: the same keys with the layers' text; finish?: hasl (default) | enig, how bare copper looks → {component, component_name, sketch, feature, body, bodies, holes, slots, skipped, thickness, offset: [x, y] added to the files' coordinates, layer_sketches?: ids, prints?: names, warnings}: a new component in the active one, named after the board, holding a sketch Outline on XY with the outline (closed loops inside it are cut-outs) and every hole and slot wholly inside the board, and one extrude of the board by its thickness as the body Board; its properties pcb.outline, pcb.drills and pcb.thickness name the files and the thickness; a hole or slot outside the board or across its edge is skipped with a warning; gaps in the outline up to 0.05 mm are closed with a line and a warning, a wider gap is refused, naming it; each layer given is kept exactly as hidden sketches in the component (Top copper, Bottom mask...) and the board gets each side's printed look (solder mask, copper, finish, silkscreen) as an image on its face, Top print and Bottom print; component properties pcb.<layer> name the layer files. A sketch being edited is finished first. One undo step

label: PCB Files
params: path: a board's files as one: a zip, a folder, or any file in the board's folder → {source, files: [{name, role: outline | drill | top_copper | bottom_copper | top_mask | bottom_mask | top_silk | bottom_silk | other}], thickness?: mm, finish?: hasl | enig, name, warnings}: what file.insert_gerber with this `set` would use; nothing changes

label: Print Face
params: body: its name; point?: [x, y, z] on a flat face of it, in mm (omit to clear) → {body, face?}: marks the face a slicer export (file.send_to_slicer, file.save_mesh with slicer, file.open_in_easyprint), or an STL or 3MF export with lay_on_print_faces (file.export, file.export_stl, file.export_3mf, file.save_mesh), lays the body on: turned so the face points down at Z = 0, the centre of mass over the origin. One per body, replacing the last; flat faces of solid bodies only. A print face that is gone or no longer flat is reported in the export's warnings, and the body exported as it lies

label: Design Properties
params: → metadata: the design's metadata object as saved (other tools' keys too); properties: each of SolidCraft's design properties (project, part number, revision…), its text or null (absent, or not text)

label: Change Design Properties
params: key and value, or values: {key: value, …} (all or nothing, one undo step). SolidCraft's keys, the ones document.metadata's properties lists, take text ("" or null removes); another tool's data goes under its reverse-DNS key such as com.example.tool (an object; null removes) → metadata, changed: [keys]

label: Remove Design Property
params: key, or keys: [keys] (any key, also one another tool wrote) → metadata, removed: [keys that were there]

label: Component Colors
params: enabled?: bool (omitted: toggle); temporary component colours, without changing appearances

label: Measure
params: bodies?: [names] (default all); names_only?: bool (each world body's name and its definition's, nothing measured) → closed per body; volume_mm3, center_of_mass, density_g_cm3 and mass_g only for closed, consistently oriented bodies; area, bbox and counts for all; total.open_bodies_skipped counts bodies excluded from volume/mass totals; or items: [1-2 selections] (face/edge: type, body, and point on it or index from model.faces/model.edges, or both) → length/area/volume; a face's perimeter_mm, with outer_perimeter_mm and inner_perimeter_mm on a flat face with holes; diameter, radius, circumference or arc_length/angle_deg of circles, arcs and cylinders; slot sizes; min (distance_mm, from, to), max, center_distance (centre to centre, or from an axis) and angle

label: Inspect Design
params: measure?: bool (include body measurements); sketch_counts?: bool (each sketch also gives its plane and its number of points and constraints); timeline?: true (default) | "summary" (each feature as id, name, type, with error, warning, suppressed and rolled_back only when set) | false (left out); bodies?: true (default) | "names" (only the body names, nothing measured) | false (left out)

label: Design Revision
params: → document_id (this open design's id: kept while it stays open, another for each design started or opened), revision (moves whenever the design, what is hidden or a component's uncaptured position changes, never on a selection or a view; from one counter for the whole run, so it never repeats). Read-only

label: Inspect Sketch
params: sketch?: id|name (default active)

label: List Edges
params: body: name

label: List Faces
params: body: name → per face: index, name (what face.delete, sheet.convert `face`, solid.shell … take in place of a point), exact, area, centroid (not always on the face), plane_normal, point (a point on the face that picks it), cylinder? ({origin, axis, radius} of a cylindrical face), sheet_face? (a folded sheet's face: `sheet:<body>:<panel>:<side>`, panel base or a flange's tag F<feature>.<k>, side top | bottom | rim.<edge> | bend.inner | bend.outer; taken wherever a face name is, and it holds while sizes change and flanges come and go)

label: List Body Features
params: body?: name (a placed copy's name means the body it shows; default every body) → bodies: [{body, features: [{id, name}]}], in timeline order the feature that created each body, every later one that changed it, and those of bodies consumed into it. Read-only

label: Physical Material
params: bodies: [names]; material: name (Steel, Aluminum, ABS Plastic, …, or one made with material.create; `material.list`)

label: Appearance
params: bodies?: [names]; faces?: [[x,y,z] on faces] (body?: which body, default the nearest); components?: [names or ids, or occurrence names]; appearance?: library name or stable starter.* ID (appearance.library) | color: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0–255), opacity? (0–1, default 1); name?: inert copied look label (requires color, mutually exclusive with appearance); pbr?: {metallic:0..1, roughness:0.045..1, dielectric_ior:1..3} (requires color/appearance and opacity 1); a starter ID or registered starter name resolves its recipe before color overrides; omitted pbr retains that response and pbr: null explicitly clears it. Unavailable glass recipes refuse through either selector. Other custom labels with an explicit color retain legacy scalar behavior. Neither appearance nor color (or color: null): clear, so the face follows its body, the body its component, the component its material

label: Copy Look
params: target: appearance.chain target. Copies its resolved look to a transient session clipboard. No document change or dialogs.

label: Paste Look
params: bodies/faces/components: appearance.assign targets. Applies the copied look atomically in one undo step; no dialogs.

label: Favorite Look
params: look: appearance.assign look; favorite: bool → validated look and preference request; UI library preference only, no document change or dialogs.

label: Appearance Chain
params: target: {body: name} | {body: name, face: zero-based model.faces index} | {component: name or id}; a placed copy's name (`KB (K:2)`, `K:2`) means the body or component it shows. Returns steps [{step: face|body|component|material, look: {name,color,opacity,pbr?} or null}] in precedence order and active (step or null). Component material is the common default look of its directly owned bodies, null if mixed/empty. Imported paint is a display fallback outside the four steps. Read-only; no dialogs

label: Replace Appearance
params: from: library name | saved look {name,color,opacity,pbr?} (copy appearance.list in_design); to: library name | assignment look {appearance? | color, name?, opacity?, pbr?} (appearance.assign rules; no clear). Matches the full look including name and PBR. scope?: {bodies?: [names], components?: [names or ids]} (a placed copy's name means the body or component it shows), at most 10000 targets; body scope includes face overrides, component scope selects only the component override. Omitted scope means all overrides, including hidden/suppressed ones; physical defaults are unchanged. Duplicate targets count once. Returns count of rewritten overrides; zero adds no history. One undo step, atomic; no dialogs. Designs above 100000 overrides refuse

label: Appearance Library
params: → 20 legacy scalar appearances, six opaque PBR finishes and 40 starter recipes with IDs, categories, provenance, requirements and availability; six starter glass recipes are unavailable

label: List Appearances
params: body?: name (or a placed copy's, `KB (K:2)`: the body it shows) → assigned appearances; with body, its resolved look and its faces' (face index, look)

label: List Materials
params: → built-in and design-owned materials (user: true, look, optional physical_card/physical_validation/density_comparison). Read-only; candidate engineering records do not certify sources or supply a solver

label: Describe Command
params: command: a command id. Returns {id, label, params, input, output} (and param_warnings in the warn parameter-check mode): the command's parameter documentation and, once the command has a typed contract, the JSON Schemas (2020-12) of its parameters and of a successful result (null otherwise). Read-only.

label: Compare Bodies
params: a, b: body names (default: the two selected bodies, or the design's only two), in world placement; tolerance?: mm (0.001 to 10, default 0.01): surfaces closer than this agree; spacing?: mm (default 0.5): the largest piece of a face sampled as one point, coarser for a body that would need more than max_points? (default 8 million, up to 50 million) samples; max_regions? (default 50); color?: true | {only_in_a?, only_in_b?: "#rrggbb"} (colours the faces that hold a region, red where only a has material and green where only b has: the faces mostly beyond the tolerance, else the one with the largest share; an undo step) → a, b: volume_mm3, area_mm2, center_of_mass, bbox; difference: b − a; deviation: a_to_b, b_to_a (max_mm, mean_mm, at, area_beyond_mm2); regions, largest first: side (only_in_a | only_in_b), volume_mm3, center and bbox (measured_by: "boolean": exact, the pieces of a − b or b − a there, measured as inspect.measure does; "not measured": the cut could not be made, so volume_mm3 and center are null and not_measured says why, never an estimate), area_mm2, max_deviation_mm, at, faces_a, faces_b (face indices, as model.faces lists them); identical; verdict; warnings (a body whose surface does not enclose what it measures, lines left out, a cut that could not be made). The regions are found from the two surfaces, so near-identical bodies compare too

label: Compare Picture
params: reference: path to a PNG or JPEG the model should match; view?/camera?/bodies?/rows? as inspect.silhouette; crop_px?: [x, y, w, h] in pixels, or crop_fraction?: [x, y, w, h] as fractions 0..1 of the picture (to take one view off a board); part_fills_crop?: false — with true the crop box is the part itself and no background search runs, for a crop that tightly frames the part; fit?: "width" | "height" | "both" (default "width"): one uniform scale, taken from the named dimension ("both" claims both and scales by width, reporting aspect_mismatch when the shapes differ); overlay?: false leaves the overlay PNG out → overlap (0..1), edges: top|bottom|left|right in mm at nine stations (positive where the model reaches past the picture, null where a station misses one of the two), the grid and its mm_per_px, and overlay_png (red model, blue picture) as base64 PNG. Preserves subject geometry, lighting, output, pose and engineering materials; one undo and rechecked product separation. Not an infinite/analytically smooth/terrain background.

label: Remove Render Stage
params: name: setup, set?: setup patch. Removes saved render-only panels atomically; CAD geometry and lighting are unchanged.

label: Save Surface Binding
params: name: CPU or GPU setup; set?: setup patch; surface: same input as render.library.surface.prepare; replace?: false. Pins exact source hashes and definition/feature/occurrence identity with local-mm mapping in one undo. No paths, mesh ordinals or physical material changes.

label: Remove Surface Binding
params: name: setup, target: saved definition/feature/component/occurrence_path, set?: setup patch. Removes only that explicit binding in one undo; no device or current geometry required.

label: Retain Displayed Render Result
params: job?: completed JobId (default selected result), or null to clear selection. Selects within the eight retained completed results; oldest is evicted first. Preserves exact export bytes and original host memory accounting. No design/undo change; preview or foreign jobs refuse.

label: Find Render Library Targets
params: query?: exact-name substring; offset?:0; limit?:128 (1..128). Returns a bounded page of captured body ordinals/names, revision and scene bounds. Settles the model through ordinary command handling; never returns a large mesh payload.

label: Browse Render Library
params: kind?: surfaces, selene_appearances, hdr, rigs, scenes, materials, lighting, environments, quality, native_scenes, selene_shots or capabilities; query?: bounded search; availability?: all/usable/specification/blocked; offset?:0; limit?:48 (1..128). Returns source status and explicit implemented projections separately. No device, file IO or design change.

label: Inspect Render Library Resource
params: kind, id: exact authored resource. Returns original specification, runtime projection variants and explicit omissions. A concept is not an executable preset.

label: Apply Library Opaque Appearance
params: id: SURF-* or SELENE-AP-*; variant: uniform_opaque (required); bodies: 1..256 exact body names. Applies the original scalar baseline through ordinary appearance assignment in one undo, preserving physical properties. Spatial maps and advanced target effects are explicitly excluded.

label: Apply Built-in HDR Environment
params: id: HDR-*; name: saved setup; set?: typed CPU/GPU setup patch; rotation_rad?: authored rotation (native origin offset is explicit in the reply); intensity?:1; samples?:16 for CPU; replace_environment?:false. Hash-verifies and embeds original bytes, saves one atomic undo without external files or a render device. An HDR-owned sun cannot duplicate an analytic sun.

label: Prepare Authored Surface Maps
params: id: SURF-*; body_index and body_name from render.scene; origin?:[0,0,0]; plane?:xy/yz/zx; scale?:1; rotation_rad?:0 (positive around the plane normal). Returns an explicit GPU temporary planar binding and a source usable by saved CPU/GPU surface.bind, with source hashes, original millimetre scale, image-up normal orientation and absolute base-color semantics. No document change; height/displacement and true anisotropy are not included.

label: Prepare Authored Studio Lights
params: id: RIG-*; variant: complete for emitter-only rigs, emitters_only for rigs with passive cards; center_mm and subject_extent_mm required. Converts exact rectangular half-edges and solar direction/radius. Optional name and typed CPU set return the complete CPU projection and explicit indirect-lighting adoption plan; authored radiance beyond CPU intensity64 refuses without scaling. Blocked calibration and external-sun rigs refuse. Returns a geometry-clearance review requirement; does not create cards or modify the scene.

label: Apply Authored Studio Lights
params: rig: id, variant, center_mm and subject_extent_mm; name; set?: typed CPU/GPU setup patch; expected_revision?:u64; enable_indirect?:false (explicit CPU Sun adoption after review); replace_lighting_and_environment:true required. Saves the explicit rig projection in one undo, removing prior lighting/environment only with that confirmation. Subject clearance still needs review; passive cards are never silently omitted.

label: Inspect HDR Source
params: path: scoped Radiance HDR file; validates the complete bounded source and returns sha256, width, height, encoded_bytes and primaries without saving or rendering

label: Save Render Settings with HDR
params: name, set: typed CPU/GPU setup patch with hdr/environment unset; path: scoped HDR; expected_sha256?: digest returned by render.hdr.inspect (changed sources refuse); rotation_rad?:0, intensity?:1; samples?:1/4/16/64 for CPU only (default16); assume_linear_srgb?:false for GPU only. Captures immutable bytes and saves resource plus setup atomically in one undo, without a host; returns name/setup/resource metadata, never source bytes

label: Check Render Request
params: setup?: saved name OR settings?: full RenderSetup. A typed job selects raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path and its numerical options plus embedded HDR before dispatch; only replace and transient studio_weights may accompany it. Without job, the legacy runtime controls below remain available. See docs/render-settings.md. studio_weights?: three finite 0..1 visibility weights for raster or implicit GPU studio sources only; never saved. integrator?: raster (default) or raytrace; progressive?: false (registered GPU path, CPU integrator/LED options are mutually exclusive); texture_filtering?: false (GPU); CPU raytrace.texture_filtering?: false. Explicitly enables ray-footprint mip and bounded anisotropic map filtering on GPU, and bounded anisotropic filtering on CPU. GPU filtering off retains bilinear LOD0; CPU filtering off retains isotropic mip selection, using the coarsest available mip when footprint data is unavailable. samples?: 1..65536; max_depth?: 1..64; seed?: u32 for progressive; raytrace?: bounded runtime progressive/primary_samples/lights/punctual_lights/area_lights/area_samples/seed/exposure_ev/shadows/reflections/anisotropic_faces/emissions/surface_effects/dielectrics/environment options, only with raytrace. CPU raytrace.lens?: {aperture_radius_mm:0..10000000,focus_distance_mm:0.000001..1000000000}; positive aperture requires explicit CPU progressive sampling and a bounded perspective camera; absent/zero keeps the original CPU ray stream. See docs/render-thin-lens.md. CPU raytrace.volume?: one HomogeneousVolume box with world-mm min_mm/max_mm, extinction_per_mm:0..1000, RGB scattering_albedo:0..1 and anisotropy:-0.95..0.95. Positive extinction requires explicit Indirect lighting and cannot combine with Glass/SSS or surface Denoise. Physical eye/pupil prefixes and the orthographic line/box union preserve camera/model framing under existing ray/profile caps. See docs/render-cpu-volume.md. CPU raytrace.sun? uses the shared finite-disk Sun contract; raytrace.sky? uses {gradient,rotation_rad,intensity}. Both require explicit Indirect lighting, and gradient Sky excludes a constant/HDR environment. Their medium NEE uses the HG response/PDF and physical light source; see docs/render-cpu-celestial.md. CPU transparent_background?:false exports straight-alpha primary geometry coverage for fixed/progressive sampling; body/face opacity must remain 1, and active bloom/backdrop/photographic effects require opaque output. CPU raytrace.output?: {tone_map,finishing,backdrop,linear_exr}; shared presentation supports up to 8192 per side and 33554432 output pixels, CPU exposure remains raytrace.exposure_ev; raw FLOAT32 EXR is retained only at final completion. CPU raytrace.budget?: compact (legacy default), studio or workstation; see docs/render-cpu-resource-profiles.md for explicit image/geometry/memory/work limits. CPU raytrace.progressive?: {samples_per_pixel:1..profile limit, seed:u32}; requires primary_samples:1 and selected reflections.samples:1; area/LED sources and certified planar anisotropy/thin-sheet/axis-aligned-box dielectric continuations share the existing bounded transport and compatibility checks. See docs/render-cpu-progressive.md; environment?: {path: scoped HDR, expected_sha256?: inspected digest, rotation_radians: 0, intensity: 1, samples: 16} OR {resource: saved HDR digest, rotation_radians, intensity, samples}; embedded resources cannot combine with path/hash; explicit sRGB/D65 HDR primaries required. Opaque CPU preview with selected mirror/rough-specular reflections and certified planar anisotropy. HDR with rough reflections or anisotropy requires fully metallic selected bodies and all effective faces; unsupported combinations refuse. Optional raytrace.path:{max_depth:1..64} enables CPU diffuse/specular GI with matched rectangle/HDR light and BSDF MIS plus certified closed-mesh Glass. It requires explicit progressive camera sampling, primary_samples:1 and traced shadows; selected reflections and certified anisotropy refuse before HDR IO without changing intent. CPU Path dielectric subsurface?:{scattering_per_mm:0..100,anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} enables homogeneous free-flight/HG walks inside certified closed media; positive rates require denoising off. Contained light connections include scattering survival; closed refractive light connections and combining Glass with external volume remain unsupported. Absent path keeps the old certified thin_sheet/closed_box producer and refuses subsurface intent explicitly. See docs/render-cpu-general-glass.md and render-raytrace-dielectrics.md. CPU emissions are visible radiance and may light neighbors through sampled Path continuation, without mesh-emitter next-event sampling; surface_effects change roughness/shading normals without geometry changes. led_strip?: continuous world-mm LED rectangle recipe; led_samples?: 1/4/16/64 for the whole strip, default16. At most8directional+8punctual+4rectangle/LED sources; shared area N. See docs/render-light-union.md. transparent_background?: false; replace?: false. With progressive:true, raytrace instead accepts GPU dielectrics/clear_coats/textures; environment instead accepts tagged hdr/embedded_hdr/sky with rotation_rad/intensity; file hdr supports expected_sha256, embedded_hdr uses a document resource digest. See docs/render-hdr-resources.md. GPU lens, studio lighting, tone_map, denoise, clamp_indirect?: 0.000001..1000000 (biased; caps each contribution from the first bounce on, keeping its hue; see docs/render-path.md), bounded finishing/backdrop and linear_exr retention are also available. CPU raytrace and GPU top-level controls accept supersampling:1|2 (default 1; doubles internal width and height at 2, averages scene-linear premultiplied samples before tone mapping, exports selected dimensions), denoise_settings:{passes:1..3,strength:0..1,firefly_suppression:bool,optical_filter:bool}, and denoise_diagnostics:false. Optical filtering defaults to true for eligible mirror/glass guides; optical_filter:false restores legacy opaque-only display denoising. Guides and diagnostics retain their independent eligibility policy and conservative highlight protection. CPU raytrace.threads:0..64 selects bounded automatic workers at 0 (default), serial work at 1 or an explicit count from 2 through 64. Resource checks include internal image buffers and worker scratch. See docs/render-quality-controls.md. Both path tracers accept optional metal_energy_compensation: true for rough isotropic metals (inside CPU raytrace or top-level GPU). Both methods accept optional caustics {photons:1..1048576,radius_mm:0.000001..1000000,max_depth:1..64,seed:u32,area_lights?:false,environment?:false,guided_emission?:false,refresh_per_pass?:false} (inside CPU raytrace; top-level GPU). Optical assignments accept optional model {roughness:0..1,dispersion?:{abbe_number:5..200},thin_film?:{ior:1..3,thickness_nm:0..100000}}. CPU advanced models require Path; rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off. See docs/render-glass-material-models.md. GPU adaptive?: {pilot_samples:16..256,min_samples:16..samples,relative_error:0..1,absolute_error:0.000001..1000000,coverage_error:0.001..0.25} allocates independent production budgets; pilots are discarded, not a certified error guarantee. transmission_samples?:1|2|4 stratifies the first Fresnel branch with extra path cost. volume?:{min_mm:[x,y,z],max_mm:[x,y,z],extinction_per_mm:0..1000,scattering_albedo:[r,g,b],anisotropy:-0.95..0.95} is one finite homogeneous world-mm medium; active media require explicit lighting/environment and refuse glass, denoise and multiple transmission strata. These fields also persist in GPU job.options. See docs/render-materials/TRANSPORT-MASTER-BATCH-2026-10-23.md; see docs/render-transmission.md, render-environment.md, render-runtime-textures.md, render-thin-lens.md, render-studio-lighting.md and render-denoise.md. Optional CPU raytracing requires a raytrace-cpu build and native host, checked before scene capture. Stale geometry is rejected. See docs/render-jobs.md

label: Render Image
params: Same request as render.preflight. Captures an immutable product scene and queues a bounded image job. Returns its session-scoped job identity, captured scene_generation and progress. Does not change the design. See docs/render-jobs.md

label: Render Progress
params: job?: {session, serial, generation}. Non-blocking progress, errors and captured frame metadata with queue:{running,waiting,job,shot,error}. Without job returns queue only. Advances an explicitly started render.batch through render.start as jobs finish; never pumps render work. Preview is separate from the exportable final image.

label: Cancel Render
params: job?: {session, serial, generation}, default the active render.batch job. Requests cooperative cancellation and drops its waiting shots; completed jobs remain completed. Late cancelled frames cannot be published.

label: Copy Render Image
params: job?: completed JobId (default selected result). Validates the retained PNG for app clipboard copying (max 4096 per side, 4194304 pixels); headless returns frame metadata only. Never copies a provisional image or starts a job.

label: Export Render Image
params: job?: {session, serial, generation} (default selected result), path: destination matching format?: png (default), exr or denoise_mask (PNG extension), overwrite?: false. Guide masks require denoise_diagnostics captured during rendering; their separate bytes, dimensions and SHA are returned under denoise_mask, while frame identifies the parent colour result. EXR requires an opt-in raw linear master retained by that completed CPU or GPU job; never converts PNG pixels. Exports a retained completed image atomically; an existing destination is preserved on failure. See docs/render-jobs.md

label: Render Backends
params: No parameters. Returns {schema_version: 1, default_backend: builtin, backends: [{id, label, availability, executors: [{id, availability, profiles, limits, scratch}]}]}. Metadata only; does not start rendering or probe a GPU. See docs/render-backends.md

label: Render Settings
params: name?: saved setup. Without name returns {setups, defaults}; with name returns {name, setup}. Does not evaluate the model or apply a camera. See docs/render-settings.md

label: Save Render Settings
params: name: setup name, set: object of fields to replace (backend, mode, camera, width, height, format, exposure_ev, environment_rotation, environment_intensity, background, job, surfaces, optics, coats, stage). job?: typed active raster/cpu_raytrace/gpu_path configuration with optional validated embedded HDR reference; omitted preserves, null clears, object replaces the complete job. Creates from defaults and saves without a host, validates atomically, one undo step; identical edits are no-ops. See docs/render-settings.md

label: Inspect Render Scene
params: No parameters. Authoritative product-scene metadata, without modelling overlays or mesh payloads. Explicitly settles stale geometry; does not render an image. See docs/render-workspace.md

label: Apply Render Camera
params: name: saved setup. Applies its existing Camera snapshot including roll/up as view state, without modifying the document or starting a render.

label: Copy Render Check Report
params: text: nonempty report, at most 65536 bytes. Validated clipboard request; headless echo only, never renders or edits a design.

label: Select Render Result
params: index: integer 0..7, oldest first; must be retained. Selects a completed result as transient per-document view state; echoes index.

label: Discard Render Result
params: index: integer 0..7, oldest first; must be retained. Drops only that transient result, selecting the newest remaining result if necessary; echoes index.

label: Set Render Output Size
params: width, height: 1..16384; custom?: bool. Validated Render output draft request; headless echo only, no design edits or job. The UI separately limits new selections to 8192 per side, 33554432 output pixels and the selected rendering profile.

label: View Render Image
params: view: model|image|fit|actual|denoise_mask. Guide-mask view requires a selected completed result captured with denoising diagnostics. Validated result canvas request; headless echo only, never starts a job.

label: Close Render Image
params: No parameters. Return to Model Preview; headless echo only, never cancels a job.

label: Paint Appearance
params: appearance or color/name/opacity/pbr: appearance.assign look parameters; validates and returns look for ui.start paint. done?: true ends the UI tool. Programmatic calls never open UI.

label: Pick Up Appearance
params: target?: appearance.chain target; returns its resolved look, or requests the UI sampling tool when omitted. Programmatic calls never open UI.

label: Solo Light
params: id?: kind:slot light address; solo:bool. Enabling requires an id; false clears solo. Validates and echoes per-document UI view state. Never saves settings, evaluates geometry, opens an editor or changes history.

label: Mute Light
params: id: kind:slot light address; mute:bool. Validates and echoes per-document UI view state, applied to live preview and captured render copies only. Never changes saved settings or history.

label: Compare Images
params: left, right: live or retained result index 0..7 (oldest first), distinct and retained; OR off:true. Validated per-document comparison view request; headless echo, no rendering or design/history change.

label: Move Render Comparison Divider
params: position: finite number, clamped to 0.05..0.95. Transient comparison divider request; headless echo only.

label: Render All Shots
params: request?: render.start parameters, shared across all saved shots except camera. Default: first saved setup in name order. Captures up to 32 shot cameras and queues sequentially through render.start; returns {queued:n}. Refuses active renders, no shots or stale geometry. render.status (also with {}) and the UI tick advance the queue; Cancel on the active job drops waiting shots. No design/history/revision change.
